data.cultural_impact: Keshar is a significant name in Hindu culture, especially in relation to Hindu deities and epic heroes. In Hindu mythology, gods like Lord Indra and Lord Vishvakarma are known to have Keshar, i.e., golden hair. Indra, the deity of rain and thunder, is often depicted with a flowing golden mane. Keshar is also mentioned in epic poems like the Mahabharata and Ramayana, where powerful heroes like Arjuna and Rama are referred to as having golden locks.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Keshar lies in the symbolism of hair representing divine grace and blessings. In Hinduism, the head is considered the most sacred part of the body, and getting someone’s touch on the head is considered a sign of respect and blessing. Having golden hair, as in the name Keshar, is believed to be a manifestation of divine blessings bestowed upon a person. Additionally, the Hindu belief of the hair being a manifestation of inner vitality, strength, and health is another spiritual meaning behind the name Keshar.
